paper.title: Biological homeostasis of the global environment: the parable of Daisyworld

headline: Watson-Lovelock Daisyworld (agent-based): 2/3 locked clauses REPRO; WITH-daisy temp range 45.3 C over the full locked grid (within the populated window only 6.9 C) vs bare-control 45.3 C; daisy mix shifts black->white as L_sol rises

verdicts.gate: P1 WITH-daisy mean-temp range over L_sol[0.7,1.3] < 10.0 C (temperature homeostasis)
reasons: WITH-daisy temp range over the full locked grid = 45.26 C (need < 10.0); daisies go extinct at the grid extremes (cold/hot death), where temperature reverts to the bare control — see the within-window range in results.json

verdicts.gate: P2 BARE-control mean-temp range over the same L_sol grid >= 30.0 C (tracks luminosity, no regulation)
P3 daisy mix shifts black-dominated (low L_sol) -> white-dominated (high L_sol)

extra.model_class: genuine agent-based, spatial: each grid cell is a Patch agent that perceives its local temperature and acts (death + colonisation); temperature regulation is EMERGENT from local selection, with no global control law
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model (the spatial agent-based analogue of the Watson-Lovelock box model); no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce temperature homeostasis and the black->white albedo shift, and would catch an artifact
extra.caveat: Homeostasis is STRONG but BOUNDED: within the populated luminosity window (where daisies persist) the WITH-daisy temperature range is only ~6.9 C while the bare control swings ~33 C — the regulation mechanism (white daisies cool / black daisies warm via local albedo selection) is clearly reproduced. But at the locked-grid EXTREMES daisies suffer cold death (too cold for the first daisies to establish) / hot death (the optimum is exceeded), and temperature reverts to the bare control. Graded on the FULL locked grid [0.7,1.3], P1's <10 C band is therefore a MISS; this is reported honestly rather than tuned away (the locked grid is wider than this model's homeostasis window). Watson & Lovelock's own Daisyworld also collapses outside a luminosity window.

citations: Watson, A.J. & Lovelock, J.E. (1983). Biological homeostasis of the global environment: the parable of Daisyworld. Tellus B 35(4):284-289. doi:10.1111/j.1600-0889.1983.tb00031.x.
Lovelock, J.E. (1983). Daisy world - a cybernetic proof of the Gaia hypothesis. CoEvolution Quarterly 38:66-72.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction. The literature anchor is temperature homeostasis over a luminosity range plus the black->white albedo shift; the spatial agent-based world reproduces both WITHIN its homeostasis window and collapses outside it (as the original does).
